html:
On 9 October 2006 North Korea set off its first nuclear explosion, underground at Punggye-ri in the northeast, becoming the eighth country known to have tested nuclear weapons.

The programme went back to a Soviet-built research reactor at Yongbyon. A 1994 deal froze it for a while, but it collapsed, and North Korea left the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty in 2003. The 2006 test was small, under one kiloton, and may have partly failed, but the point was made. The United Nations Security Council answered with sanctions.

Five more tests followed up to 2017, the last a thermonuclear device far larger. With missiles, they made the bomb the centre of the state under Kim Jong Il and Kim Jong Un, and an answer to the fate of states that gave up their weapons. A test in 2016 led South Korea to close the Kaesong zone.
sum: On 9 October 2006 North Korea set off its first nuclear explosion, underground at Punggye-ri in the northeast, becoming the eighth country known to have tested nuclear weapons.
